name: Drought
value: Sudan harvest failure; no famine declared
summary: Crop Monitor rates Sudan's main-season crops a failure after record-dry rains; no drought famine declaration found
state: GEOGLAM's Crop Monitor of 5 Nov rates Sudan's main-season crops a failure after late, below-average rains and conflict, ranks June–September the driest on record across much of South Sudan, and reports drought in northern Ethiopia, the Sahel and South Africa's Western Cape wheat region (Crop Monitor). The IPC warned on 12 Oct of rising famine risk in Sudan's conflict areas (Reuters via TimesLIVE, 23 Oct). Sudan is not a major exporter, so severe drought in crop regions keeps Watch; searches on 18 Nov found no new drought-driven famine declaration.
for_you: Most exposed are households in Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia and the Sahel, where poor harvests tend to raise local food prices and aid needs. Little direct effect on UK food supply is expected.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in major crop regions (Sudan harvest failure, East Africa, Sahel); no famine declaration or major exporter failure for Alert

sources.title: GEOGLAM — Crop Monitor for Early Warning, November 2026
TimesLIVE (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
